subject: English
central_question: How can a student choose determiners that correctly express definiteness, distance, possession, quantity and number before nouns?
in_scope_units: Demonstratives this, that, these and those
Quantifiers with countable and uncountable nouns

known_pitfalls.claim: Using many with an uncountable noun such as water.
known_pitfalls.correction: Use much with uncountable nouns; many is used with countable nouns.

known_pitfalls.claim: Writing an university because university begins with the letter u.
known_pitfalls.correction: Use a university because the word begins with the consonant sound "yoo".

known_pitfalls.claim: Omitting the in "He is best student."
known_pitfalls.correction: Use "He is the best student" in the reference superlative pattern.

recommended_example_progression: Match this/that/these/those to distance and number
Choose quantifiers for countable or uncountable nouns and some/any patterns
Contrast each and every and correct mixed determiner errors
ncert_end_of_chapter_exercises_reference: Typical CBSE practice includes filling blanks with suitable determiners, correcting article and quantifier errors, and choosing forms based on number, countability and context.
